mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% month-over-month, sustained for two months, signals supply-side stress that raises input costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM change < -3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes of two consecutive months of >3% MoM INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their prior 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime that erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust residential demand, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12M MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (UNRATE > 5% AND PAYEMS YoY change < -1%) signals a deepening labor market downturn, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where both UNRATE exceeds 5% and PAYEMS falls by more than 1% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent, broad-based decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by the sum of GDPC1 and RSAFS, both in real terms) over three consecutive quarters signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Three consecutive quarterly declines in combined real income proxies (GDPC1 + RSAFS)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive quarterly declines in combined real income (GDPC1 + RSAFS).
